title: Delimiter spectra harmonizer and chat-template runner for onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During recent onboarding of several open models we observed a systematic latency regression for chat-style prompts after model version pinning and performance profile publishing. Root cause analysis indicates two interacting issues: (1) tokenizer delimiter normalization produced a different distribution of tokenized prefix/suffix lengths than the sample corpus used for the model's perf profile, and (2) published perf profiles lacked a compact representation of the tokenization "delimiter spectra" (role markers, system prompts, multi-line delimiters) used by chat templates. This caused the runtime's batching and kernel-selection heuristics to choose suboptimal paths for real traffic.

Goal: Create a harmonization layer and a lightweight onboarding probe that captures delimiter/tokenization spectra and chat-template framing statistics, include these in the model perf profile, and add backward-compatible fallbacks so older runtimes won't break. This should prevent version-pinning + profile publishing from inadvertently increasing tail latency or altering throughput.

Proposed implementation:
1) delimiter-spectra library: implement a small, dependency-free module (go/python) that runs tokenization over canonical chat templates and computes distribution buckets for: leading-role-length, system-prefix-length, trailing-delimiter-variance, token-escape-rate. Expose a compact JSON array (stringified) intended for perf profiles (field name: delimiter_spectra_v1).
2) onboarding probe: integrate the library into the onboarding pipeline (model-bundle-builder) so that after tokenization checks we run the probe against the golden template set and the model's tokenizer. The probe will produce microbenchmarks and histograms and a checksum.
3) perf profile publishing: extend the profile schema to accept delimiter_spectra_v1 and sequence_length_cdf (coarse buckets). Update the publisher to sign and publish the extended profile alongside existing metrics.
4) runtime/compat: update runtime heuristics to prefer explicit spectra when present, but fall back to legacy heuristics when not. Add a compatibility shim so older profiles are interpreted as 'generic' with conservative batching settings.
5) tests & CI: add unit tests for the library, integration tests in onboarding CI to ensure profiles include spectra for pinned rollouts, and an end-to-end microbenchmark job that simulates common chat traffic and verifies SLOs.
6) rollout plan: canary publish profiles for a small % of traffic (Dedicated + Hosted) and compare latency/throughput. If regressions detected revert to fallback policy and block profile publish with an automated alert.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: tokenizer reworks or broader tokenizer/shim projects. This is a targeted change focused on profile telemetry and onboarding pipelines.

acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline publishes perf profiles that include delimiter_spectra_v1 and sequence_length_cdf for all newly pinned models
Runtime uses spectra for batching/kernel selection when present and demonstrates no >5% tail-latency regression vs baseline in canary
Backward compatibility: older runtimes consume profiles without spectra and apply safe defaults
Unit and integration tests added to CI; onboarding smoke test fails the build if spectra generation is missing for pinned publishes
